newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent rallies strongly but wet North Sea lags.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent rallies strongly but wet North Sea lags.

text.p: Cash Brent crude rallied sharply on Monday, bolstered by talk of thin North Sea supply next month, but the strength failed to work through into spot markets, traders said.

The release this week of June loading programmes refocussed attention on the prospects of a sharp drop in output due to scheduled maintenance, pushing the prompt June/July intermonth spread out to +16 cents from +8 cents.
July/August gained four cents to trade at +7 cents.
"The maintenance story was so old that people were ignoring it and were caught short on the spreads," said a trader.
A jump in outright values -- June IPE Brent gained 67 cents to $19.60 a barrel by 1744 GMT -- fuelled by Middle East tension and fund buying on NYMEX helped firm sentiment.
Brent CFDs added 14 cents, this week's dates talking at July Brent +5/+7 cents. The sole Brent nominated May 27-29 loading dates on Friday was kept by Shell UK.
Dated Brent was offered at the equivalent of July +5/+10 cents a barrel but other grades struggled to move higher with Oseberg and Gullfaks C trading at steady levels, traders said.
"Clearly the market is firm... but the margins have disappeared so I don't know if this can be sustained," said one.
Mediterranean crude oil markets were steady to firmer as healthy refining margins held, refiners said.
"There are quite a few refiners who need to buy soon. The margins are not the best I have seen in my life but they are very good," one refiner said.

Despite Urals sales last week around Dated Brent -$1.18 a barrel some traders said the market was stronger than last done and one claimed he saw five buyers at Dated Brent -$1.10. Even refiners said the market was stronger than Friday's deals one of which was distressed and the other ex-Odessa.
"The market is not that low," said a refinery trader.
Good buying from the East and interest from the U.S. continued to support West African crudes. Light Nigerian grades were assessed around Dated +50 cents, Forcados at +10/15 cents.

Margins have however been eroded in the past few days in the U.S. and one refiner said current levels on both North Sea Brent and Nigerian Forcados were too high as their refining margins had taken a "hammering" in the last few days.
"The differentials will slip in the next two or three weeks. If the first decade (North Sea) loadings are not light it could be sooner than that," he said.
